summary: The history of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. From lunar rovers to Mars landers, these mechanical relics are often viewed as space junk.
details:
Project Overview & Working
Our project, "Abandoned but not Forgotten," is an interactive storytelling platform that breathes life into the history of NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars. It acts as a digital museum and narrative experience, exploring the silent rovers, landers, and descent stages left behind. Users can navigate through a timeline or a 3D visual map to discover where these historical artifacts rest and read their compelling "biographies."
Benefits & Intended Impact
This project transforms raw space data into engaging human stories, making space history accessible and exciting for students and space enthusiasts. Its intended impact is to inspire curiosity about space exploration, preserve the historical legacy of humanity's early interplanetary footprints, and spark conversations about the artifacts we leave behind in space.
Tools & Technologies Used
We developed this project using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the interactive web frontend, along with WebGL/Three.js to create the visual representations of the lunar and Martian surfaces. We also gathered historical data and coordinates directly from official NASA open-source archives and mission logs.
Creativity & Team Considerations
What makes our project unique is its creative perspective: instead of viewing these items as "space junk," we treat them as monumental historical landmarks, using a narrative-driven approach to tell their stories from their own "point of view." While designing this, our team carefully focused on user experience (UX) to ensure smooth navigation, historical accuracy, and lightweight web performance so it runs smoothly on any device.
